overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by late response to a minutes request, delayed release of executive session minutes, and an inaccurate vote record; it found no violation on purpose or notice, and declined other allegations.

allegations.summary: Board failed to review, approve, and release executive session minutes once the litigation purpose had ended, delaying release for months.
allegations.key_passage: Ultimately, the Board did not vote to approve the May 28, 2015 executive session minutes until the October 22, 2015 meeting, nearly five months after the meeting at issue.

allegations.summary: Board did not respond within 10 days to the complainant's request for executive session minutes, and waited 14 days to respond.
allegations.key_passage: To be in compliance, the Board should have notified Mr. Hawkinson within ten days that it would not be releasing the May 28, 2015 executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly entered executive session on October 22, 2015 for an improper purpose.
allegations.key_passage: By listing the litigation matter for which the May 28, 2015 executive session was convened, the meeting notice complied with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Posted meeting notice for October 22, 2015 was allegedly inaccurate due to a wrong docket number digit.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this meeting notice, despite this minor typographical error, substantially complied with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.

allegations.summary: May 28, 2015 executive session minutes allegedly lacked specificity; they called the entry vote unanimous but listed only four of six members voting.
allegations.key_passage: Because of this incongruity, members of the public cannot know, for example, if any Board members voted against the motion to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged improper redaction of executive session minutes on attorney-client privilege grounds.
allegations.key_passage: However, we decline to consider certain other allegations concerning the sufficiency of redacted executive session minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged bifurcated posting of meeting notices and a stenographer's equipment setup failure during a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, these allegations would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25. As such, we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged the Board has failed to periodically review its executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations, see OML 2012-106, and we decline to review this allegation here.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend, within thirty days, the May 28, 2015 executive session minutes to clarify the inaccuracy.
